definition: The Overhead Imagery Research Data Set (OIRDS) is a collection of an open-source, annotated, overhead images that computer vision researchers can use to aid in the development of algorithms.
details: Most computer vision and machine learning algorithms function by training on a large set of example data. Further, for many academic and industry researchers, the availability of truth-labeled test data helps drive algorithm research. While a great deal of terrestrial imagery is available on the Internet from various sources, there are few (if any) repositories of overhead imagery. The limited overhead imagery that is found via sources such as Google Earth or Google Maps is copyrighted or may have limited use.

explainer.lead: The Overhead Imagery Research Data Set is an open-source, annotated collection of overhead images for computer vision researchers. It fills a gap, since most available overhead imagery is copyrighted or otherwise restricted.

tiers.eli5: It is a shared pack of aerial photos with labels, so researchers can practice teaching computers to read them.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers train and benchmark detection algorithms on it, relying on the truth labels for evaluation. A pitfall is assuming it covers the variety of real overhead imagery, since repositories of such data are few.
tiers.paperLevel: OIRDS is defined as an open-source, annotated overhead image collection for algorithm development; no specific size, classes, or resolution figures are given.

explainer.example: A researcher trains a vehicle-detection model on labeled OIRDS images and measures accuracy against the provided annotations.
